record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.context_brief: Necessity of spectral conditions in linear iteration
record.original_question: Consider the iterative equation Σ_{j=0}^N a_j φ^j(x) = 0 on (0,∞), where φ^j denotes the j-th iterate of φ, and let c > 0 be a positive root of the characteristic polynomial Σ_{j=0}^N a_j λ^j = 0. A theorem in the paper shows that if (i) c is a simple root, (ii) there are no other positive roots, and (iii) every other root λ satisfies |λ| > c, then the only solution on a positive domain is φ(x) = cx. The open problem is whether these three conditions are actually necessary for uniqueness of the continuous or monotone solution φ:(0,∞)→(0,∞) of this iterative equation.

evidence.quote: It is an open problem whether conditions (i)–(iii) are necessary for the uniqueness of the (continuous, monotonic) solution ϕ : (0,∞) → (0,∞) of (3.2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N \ge 2$ be an integer and let $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_N \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a_N 
eq 0$. For a self-map $\varphi:(0,\infty)	o(0,\infty)$ denote by $\varphi^j$ its $j$-th iterate (with $\varphi^0(x)=x$). Consider the linear iterative functional equation
$$\sum_{j=0}^{N} a_j\,\varphi^j(x) = 0, \qquad x \in (0,\infty). \quad (\star)$$
Assume that the characteristic polynomial $P(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{N} a_j\lambda^j$ admits a positive real root $c>0$ satisfying the following three conditions:

(i) $c$ is a simple root of $P$;
(ii) $c$ is the only positive real root of $P$;
(iii) every other (complex) root $\lambda$ of $P$ satisfies $|\lambda|>c$.

Under (i)–(iii) it is known that the only continuous (equivalently monotonic) solution $\varphi:(0,\infty)	o(0,\infty)$ of $(\star)$ is the linear map $\varphi(x)=cx$.

Problem: Determine whether the conditions (i), (ii), and (iii) are necessary for the uniqueness of a continuous (respectively, monotonic) solution $\varphi:(0,\infty)	o(0,\infty)$ of equation $(\star)$. More precisely, decide whether, whenever the equation $(\star)$ has a unique continuous (or monotonic) positive solution $\varphi(x)=cx$ with $c>0$ a root of $P$, the polynomial $P$ must satisfy all three of (i), (ii), (iii); if not, exhibit a counterexample or characterize the precise spectral conditions that are equivalent to uniqueness.
